children.name: Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows
children.blurb: Agentic drafting and multi-model workflows in literary arts and narrative design refer to the practice of using software agents that can plan, draft, revise, and coordinate text across different generative models.

children.name: Outlining and Plot Structure
children.blurb: Outlining and plot structure in AI-assisted narrative design covers the use of language models to generate, refine, and test story outlines, beat sheets, act breaks, and scene sequences for fiction, screenwriting, games, and interactive narratives.

children.name: Character Voice and Dialogue
children.blurb: Character voice and dialogue in AI covers the modeling, generation, and editing of a character's distinct speech patterns, including word choice, rhythm, idiom, and conversational habits.

children.name: World-Building and Continuity
children.blurb: This page covers the use of AI to create, organize, and check the internal consistency of fictional worlds across novels, serial fiction, games, and screenwriting.

children.name: Developmental Editing
children.blurb: Developmental editing is the structural work on a manuscript or narrative: shaping plot, character arcs, pacing, point of view, theme, and overall architecture before line editing or copyediting.

sections.body: This field applies artificial intelligence to the craft of long-form fiction and narrative writing. It includes systems that draft prose from prompts or outlines, generate plot structures, write character dialogue, track continuity across a manuscript, and perform developmental editing. The work is practical, not theoretical: writers use these tools to produce chapters, test scenes, and revise drafts. Agentic drafting means the model can act on a plan, not just answer a single prompt, and multi-model workflows route different parts of a project to different models. The pages in this section describe how those pieces operate in real writing projects.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the work is uneven. Drafting and dialogue generation are widely available and can produce fluent text quickly, but they still require human oversight for plot logic, emotional truth, and originality. Outlining tools can suggest useful structures, yet they often default to familiar templates and miss the specific needs of a given story. Continuity tracking is improving but remains error-prone for long manuscripts, especially with many characters, locations, and timelines. Developmental editing tools can flag pacing problems or repeated phrases, but they do not reliably understand theme, subtext, or the reader's emotional arc. The honest limit is that these systems assist a writer's judgment, they do not replace it.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows to see how a draft gets produced and how different models are assigned to different tasks. Outlining and Plot Structure explains the earlier stage of shaping a story before prose is written, and it connects to drafting because the outline feeds the agent. Character Voice and Dialogue focuses on a narrower craft problem, making each character sound distinct, and it relies on the continuity work described in World-Building and Continuity. That page covers the tracking of facts, places, and timelines that keeps a long narrative coherent. Developmental Editing sits at the end of the process, where a completed draft is reviewed for structure, pacing, and clarity, and it often sends the writer back to the outlining or drafting pages for revision.
